card.name: Pronoun before clarifying what is meant
card.fires_on: The subject word (they, we, I) or a nearby word right after a phrase being quoted or clarified, where the next words say what is meant or referred to, as in "when we say X, we mean Y".

modes.label: Speaker clarifies meaning
modes.description: A pronoun after a quoted or stated phrase, just before "mean" or "are referring to".
modes.example: Maybe when one says that "if you don't vote you can't complain"<< they>> mean to say "only those who vote

modes.label: Clarifying a term or reference
modes.description: A word or punctuation mark closing a named term, right before "he was referring to" or "I meant".
modes.example: The “War<<”>> he was referring to was, of course

card.writes: It favors words that continue a clarification of meaning; the suppressed Chinese purpose phrases ("是为了", "只是为了") hint at a narrow semantic effect.
card.plain: It fires on the word just before someone explains what they actually meant by a phrase.
